revision_note: Post self-audit correction of v5.2.0. Pre-audit headline 0.7708 retracted (holdout slicing bug). See report_v5_2.md section 0.
research_question: Can a detector identify computational substrate independent of generator, quantization, and observation model?

loo_substrate.note: precision-level substrates at chance; strong-quantization ones visible

world_prime.interpretation: detected AS QUANTIZATION (short prime-fractional ladder), not as primality; blind holdout, non-matched control

interpretation: The detector identifies quantization artifacts (discrete value levels) but cannot identify computational substrate. When histogram statistics are matched (both monotonic and non-monotonic variants), performance collapses to chance. Pairwise same-generator/same-seed/different-substrate testing shows zero discriminative power. Novel computational mechanisms that preserve the value distribution (hash, XOR) are entirely undetected. World_PRIME is detected only because the prime-fractional ladder is visibly quantized, which confirms rather than refutes the failure mode.
key_findings: V5.1's 97.5% and pre-audit V5.2's 77.08% were both inflated; corrected generator-disjoint headline is 61.25% [55.42%, 67.50%]
Histogram matching completely defeats the detector (0.50 under both matched variants)
Pairwise substrate discrimination is impossible (0.50 on 240 controlled pairs)
S_HASH and S_UNKNOWN_COMPUTATIONAL recall: 0% (the pre-audit 8% figure came from an unbalanced test)
Feature information is generator-dominant (MI 0.36 vs substrate MI 0.15); float64_float16_diff alone identifies the generator perfectly
uint8/uint4/noise observation channels destroy all detection power
Only the computational feature family carries signal (+17.92% permutation degradation)

headline_correction.cause: holdout comp slice concentrated in single generator; G09/G10 had zero computational test samples

next_gate: DO NOT proceed to real-world data. V5.2 gate (spec section 67) requires survival of matched-statistic, pairwise, and unknown-substrate controls; all fail.
